claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is a random BCC solid solution.
The random HfNbTaTiZr state has severe local lattice distortion and a broad, low-frequency phonon DOS.
Thermal treatment can induce HfTi and TiZr B2-like clusters and percolating SRO pathways in HfNbTaTiZr.
There is a processing-temperature window that activates SRO-forming diffusion while avoiding macroscopic phase separation and brittle secondary-phase precipitation.
Keeping oxygen below 0.1 wt.% prevents embrittlement and oxygen-related defect scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
B2-like HfTi and TiZr clusters create a more periodic potential and locally reduce atomic-size-mismatch variance and lattice distortion.
The transition from random chemical disorder to ordered binary clusters reduces the RMS lattice distortion.
Reduced lattice distortion shifts the high-frequency phonon DOS to higher energies because of effective bond stiffening.
The DOS shift associated with ordering increases phonon group velocity.
The ordered clusters themselves act as phonon-scattering centers.
Background lattice distortion is the primary phonon-scattering source in random high-entropy alloys.
Percolating SRO pathways preferentially enhance transport by high-frequency phonons.
The reduction of background distortion and formation of percolating pathways outweigh cluster scattering, increasing phonon mean free path and lattice thermal conductivity.
The ordered/SRO state will show a higher lattice thermal conductivity than the random state.
The ordered/SRO state will have a lower Debye-Waller factor and smaller atomic displacement amplitudes than the random state.
Large incoherent precipitates or brittle secondary phases would restore strong scattering and reduce thermal conductivity.
Brittle C14 Laves phases in a related multi-principal-element alloy increase cracking tendency.
Oxygen above 0.65 wt.% causes cracking and defect accumulation that dominate transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Similar vacancy and self-interstitial mobilities in W-Ta-Cr-V maximize recombination and reduce defect clustering.
Ordered precipitates have been demonstrated in the stated Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti comparison system.
